messages:
Erin Lowe: Thinking aloud 1% of new signups next week get a welcome newsletter. Want to pilot two creative directions: 'Benchmark Digest' (data-driven, highlights recent quant wins) vs 'How-to Quickstart' (product tips + micro-tutorials). Goal: see which drives higher newsletter->webinar RSVP and 7-day active usage. Thoughts? :bulb:

Vikram Shah: Love the split. Suggest implementing as a true A/B with stratified sampling on signup source (organic, paid, partner). Otherwise channel bias will confound results.

Leah Kim: Agree on stratification. Also propose adding a third small holdout cell (5%) that gets a plain-text nudge from the success team to measure channel lift. Keep test cells ~30%/30%/35%/5%? (two creative, one control, one holdout)

Tess (Events): For webinar routing: RSVP flow should tag source=email_variant and signup_source so we can route hot leads to priority follow-up. Can we also prefill the RSVP form with a UTM and lead score param?

Erin Lowe: Yes to prefill. We need utm_campaign=launch_digest_split, email_variant=D|H|C|S, signup_src=organic|paid|partner, lead_score param (0-100).

Vikram Shah: Timing rec: Welcome send at T+2 hours post-signup, follow-up (if opened but no RSVP) at T+36h. Also a shorter SMS reminder for high lead_score > 70 at T+24h if no RSVP. Ensure SMS opt-in check.

Leah Kim: Copy guidelines: 1) Benchmark Digest variant = headline data point + one short quote from our benchmark report; 2) How-to Quickstart = 3 bullets + 1 inline code snippet example; both <= 130 words. Subject length <= 55 chars.

Erin Lowe: Draft subject candidates:
D1: "New benchmark: inference cost tradeoffs you should see"
D2: "Benchmarks + short Q&A: save your seat"
H1: "5-minute quickstart for your trial"
H2: "Ship your first integration in under 10 min"

Vikram Shah: Recommend D2 vs H1 as primary A/B. Keep variants D1/H2 as exploratory in smaller sub-cells. Don't reuse identical CTAs across variants; Benchmark -> "See the numbers + RSVP", How-to -> "Start the 5-min guide".

Deliverability Bot: automated: Domain health check: SPF/DKIM pass; throttle recommendation: 50/min initial then ramp. Recent complaint_rate: 0.03%. Seed check advised.

Sam (Growth): Measurement plan: primary = RSVP rate @ D7; secondary = D7 active usage; tertiary = D14 conversion. Use uplift vs control and per-source stratified lifts. I'll prep dashboard filters by email_variant & signup_src.

Leah Kim: Design asks: single hero image for Benchmark (graph snapshot), compact code block for How-to (inline). Mobile-first layout, CTA above the fold. Also include a tiny preference link: "Prefer product tips? toggle here" so users can self-select and we can learn preference signals.

Erin Lowe: Ops checklist: (1) Create stratified cohorts (Vikram), (2) Implement prefilled RSVP params + landing page capacity check (Tess), (3) Add UTM & event tags: utm_campaign=launch_digest_split, email_variant, signup_src, lead_score (Leah to add to copy), (4) Seed list + deliverability test 24h prior (Ben to run).

Vikram Shah: I'll share the SQL to generate cohorts and the randomization seed. Example: ```WITH signups AS (SELECT id, source, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY created_at) as rn FROM users WHERE created_at > DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 7 DAY)) SELECT id, CASE WHEN rn % 100 <= 30 THEN 'D' WHEN rn % 100 <= 60 THEN 'H' WHEN rn % 100 <= 95 THEN 'C' ELSE 'S' END as cell FROM signups;```

Tess (Events): Landing page will accept prefilled params. I'll check GA and RSVP ingestion. If >500 RSVPs/min, we should enable queueing.

Deliverability Bot: automated: Recommended seeds: ops@redwood.ai, sales-seed@redwood.ai, 50 external VIPs. Monitor hard_bounce>1% and complaint>0.1% as kill signals.

Sam (Growth): Quick experiments note: also capture post-click behavior on the landing page (time on page, doc downloads) to see quality of traffic, not just RSVP. We'll mark high-quality as >2min or download=1.

Erin Lowe: Timeline: Drafts by Wed EOD, design by Thu noon, seed check Thu 5pm, go/no-go Fri 9am, send Fri 11am PST. Can ops create jitter +/- 20m inside each batch?

Vikram Shah: Yes I'll implement jitter and escalate cohort A (benchmarks) to priority webhook so landing loads faster for those clicking RSVP.

Leah Kim: I'll upload both HTML + plain-text variants and the short code snippet example tonight.

Tess (Events): I'll provision RSVP seats and add webhook for immediate attendee tag to CRM. Also will create a "webinar_hot_lead" list for follow-up.

Erin Lowe: Action items recap:
- Vikram: stratified cohorts + jitter + SQL (Vikram)
- Leah: copy + upload HTML/plain text + subject lines (Leah)
- Tess: landing + RSVP ingest + capacity check (Tess)
- Ben/Deliverability: seed sends + monitor (Deliverability Bot / Ben)
- Sam: KPI dashboard + post-click quality metrics (Sam)

Erin Lowe: If all green, we'll scale to 50k sends next month based on lift. Thanks team 389
